title: Canary Quotient Quickflow & Rollforward Prototype
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: As Redwood grows, product teams need a fast, objective way to launch controlled canaries and pivot without manual orchestration. Current rollout UX captures staged traffic splits but lacks a compact, low-friction overlay for quick canaries and an explicit 'rollforward' path when a variant shows positive signal.

Objective: Design a compact Quickflow overlay in the Console that lets engineers and PMs start a short-lived canary (1–24h) with traffic 'quotient' control, safety gates wired to telemetry, and a one-click rollforward option. The overlay should minimize cognitive load for repeat power users while exposing enough controls for safety-conscious enterprise users.

Key features in this prototype:
- Canary Quotient slider and discrete presets (1%, 5%, 10%, 25%) with keyboard accessible input.
- Timebox selector (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, Custom) that drives autoschedule and end-of-canary behavior.
- Safety gates panel that anchors telemetry assertions (latency P50/P95, error rate, cost per token) with configurable thresholds and enforcement: warn vs block.
- Preview Simulator: runs a lightweight simulation using historical metrics to estimate expected cost delta and SLO risk for the selected quotient/timebox.
- Rollforward action: if telemetry shows positive uplift (configurable signals), Rollforward increases traffic to a preset target and promotes variant; includes audit message and rollback guard timer.
- Emergency rollback shortcut exposed as a sticky action with prefilled reason templates.
- Compact history strip showing last 3 canaries for the model/route with one-tap re-run.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Default presets to reduce micro-config fatigue vs. exposing fine-grain controls for power users.
- Build simulation client-side with sampling data to avoid telemetry API costs vs. server-side fidelity. Chose a hybrid: quick client estimate + link to full telemetry in Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype screens and flow (Start Canary overlay -> Safety Gate config -> Live monitor view -> Rollforward/rollback actions) in Figma.
- Usability test (5 internal engineers + 3 PMs) with <15% critical task failure rate for starting a canary and initiating a rollforward.
- Engineering sign-off on telemetry hooks and minimal API additions (2 new API fields: canary_quotient, rollforward_policy).
- A short handoff doc for Eng and PM with example API payloads and rollout audit log schema.
comments: 2026-02-21 — Ava Chen: Initial concept wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focused on minimizing modal depth and keeping rollout core actions visible. Asked Eng to estimate telemetry API changes.
2026-02-24 — Diego Marquez: Reviewed mocks; requested adding explicit cost estimate in the simulator and making the Rollforward confirmation include a countdown for immediate cancellation.
2026-03-02 — Priya Nair (PM): Validated presets and timeboxes against common use cases. Suggested default safety gates for enterprise orgs and a toggle to reveal advanced assertions.
2026-03-04 — Jonas K. (Eng): Technical review — proposed adding 'canary_quotient' and 'end_at' fields to rollout API; flagged need for a debounce on slider updates to avoid excessive backend writes.
2026-03-06 — Security (via comment): Confirmed no new sensitive scopes introduced; asked that audit messages use KMS-backed logging. Marked for optional security review for enterprise bundles.

2026-03-09 — Usability testing lead: Ran 8 internal sessions. Findings: users expect the simulator to show '95% CI cost delta' text and prefer a keyboard shortcut to re-open last canary. Updated prototype accordingly.
2026-03-10 — Diego Marquez: Marked design 'In Review' and requested engineering estimates for the API changes and a small backend job to produce simulation summaries for accurate previews.
decision_points: Keep default presets (1,5,10,25) to reduce friction; advanced slider for exact percentages
Hybrid simulation approach: client quick-estimate, server-run detailed report on demand
Expose rollforward as a first-class action when positive telemetry crosses a configurable threshold
